text:
monica: Quick design check — thinking about making compare table rows collapsible on narrow screens and adding a swipe-to-reveal actions pattern on mobile. Also want to move performance badges into the row header when collapsed. Thoughts?

sam: +1 to collapsible rows. Main risk is discoverability — users might not notice rows can expand. We should surface a chevron and a small hint in the header (e.g., ‘Tap to expand’). :speech_balloon:

anya: Agree. For mobile, swipe-to-reveal is common, but we need to be careful about conflicting gestures with horizontal carousels elsewhere. Maybe only allow vertical swipe to expand and a long-press for actions?

tj: Accessibility note: whatever we do must be keyboard and screen-reader friendly. Use a single toggle button per row with aria-expanded and a clear aria-label. Example: 
```
<button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="row-42-details">Show details for Llama-2-13B</button>
```
Also ensure the chevron is not the only affordance — hit target > 44px.

monica: Good call. UX question: when collapsed, should performance badges persist in the header (small icons) or move into the details panel? I lean to keeping small badges visible so users can scan performance at a glance.

ben: Keep badges visible. But switch to condensed badge variants (single-letter or color dot + tooltip) at narrow widths to reduce noise. We should also avoid color-only indicators for perf state because of contrast/a11y.

mike: For the condensed badges, propose tooltip on long-press or focus. Also suggestion: introduce a badge legend at top of the table that can be toggled (collapse legend to save vertical space).

anya: Another tiny a11y nit: focus outline disappears on our current row hover—ensure focus styling is preserved for keyboard users. Also aria-live for when we expand/collapse so SR users know content changed.

sam: Implementation risk: expanding many rows could blow up DOM and hurt client performance. Maybe virtualize row details and only render detail panel when expanded. Also cap max height with internal scroll for very long details.

monica: Good points. For the swipe actions (e.g., pin version, compare, open model page) — I prefer we keep primary actions in the header and secondary actions in swipe/overflow. Primary should be visible without extra gestures.

tj: Keyboard mapping: Enter toggles expand, Space opens a context menu, Arrow keys navigate rows. Make sure role="row" and role="grid" semantics are respected for screen readers.

ben: Tiny copy tweak: instead of `Tap to expand` let's use `Show model details` — clearer for SRs.

monica: Action items: 1) @sam prototype collapsible/virtualized rows (mobile + desktop) 2) @anya a11y checklist (aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-live, focus styles) 3) @ben condensed badge designs + colorblind-safe palette 4) @mike tooltip/legend patterns. I'll update the figma and post a new link later.

mike: OK will mock legend and condensed badges. ETA EOD tomorrow.

sam: I'll spike virtualization + swipe gesture detection, keep gestures opt-in behind a feature flag. ETA early next week.

monica: Thanks team — looks like a plan. If anyone sees a conflict with other mobile gestures in explorer, flag it here. :thumbsup:
